correctness.rationale: For the globally Lipschitz vector field ẋ=v, v̇=w, ẇ=−Aw−v+|x|−1, the explicitly rederived G,H satisfy Ġ=w²−v² and Ḣ=−Aw²−sgn(x)v² away from the switch; a smooth |x| regularization plus the kinetic-zero-on-x=0 lemma legitimate invariant-generator integration. Thus stationary K=∫v²=∫w² and (A+1)∫_{x>0}v²+(A−1)∫_{x<0}v²=0. Strict sign |A|>1 excludes non-equilibrium compact measures; monotone L=H+AG, integrability of v² and omega-limit connectedness prove convergence of each bounded forward orbit. At A=±1 any stationary typical complete orbit other than the opposite isolated equilibrium lies wholly in the harmonic halfspace; boundedness in both time directions eliminates exponential modes and |x| sign confinement is equivalent to radius≤1. Invariant measures there are Haar-angle mixtures. On any bounded forward critical orbit L is monotone with a finite limit, constant on its omega-limit set, equal to r²−1/2 on circles and 1/2 at the isolated opposite equilibrium; connectedness resolves the sole r=1 tie. A nonconstant periodic orbit has zero-mean v, ∫w²=∫v², and Wirtinger gives T≥2π, while equality substitution gives exclusively the indicated A=±1 circles (r>0). The proof is global analytic, not a finite enumeration.

value.rationale: For the historically central piecewise-linear Linz–Sprott jerk, the A=±1 transitions are canonical spectral/recurrence boundaries, not arbitrary parameter slices. The complete set of endpoint compact stationary measures as a simplex of circle Haar laws and one opposite equilibrium, with exact radius-one grazing cutoff and unique omega-limit radius for every bounded forward orbit, provides substantive global information unavailable from the earlier local eigenvalue or segment algorithm. The explicit exceptional bounded A=−1 circles also refine the original broad claim of negative-A divergence. The generic period lower bound is useful corroboration but not the main new value.
residual_risks: No proof of attraction from every initial condition, stability of endpoint circles, or an all-parameter compact-measure phase diagram for −1<A<1.
The standard derivative-energy period bound alone would be too routine as a standalone contribution; value rests on the global critical measure and omega-limit classification.

limitations: Compact invariant-measure classification proved only for |A|≥1, not for |A|<1.
Omega-limit radius selection applies to bounded forward orbits; no claim all critical orbits bounded or of asymptotic phase convergence.
No claimed novelty for general derivative-energy/slope identities or the generic Wirtinger period floor.
The closely relevant 2000 no-chaos paper remained abstract-only; noncoverage of its full text was not asserted.
